verses.sa: अहं वैश्वानरो भूत्वा प्राणिनां देहमाश्रितः । प्राणापानसमायुक्तः पचाम्यन्नं चतुर्विधम् ॥
verses.tr: I become the digestive fire within living beings, joined with the outgoing and incoming breaths, and digest the four kinds of food.
verses.angle: Prana and apana join the fire to digest food
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna moves from nature to the body. He is the fire that digests food inside every living being, working through the breath.

body.text: I become the digestive fire within living beings, joined with the outgoing and incoming breaths, and digest the four kinds of food. The word prana-apana means the inward and outward breaths. Krishna says this fire that digests food is joined with the breath that keeps the body alive. He then says that memory and knowledge also come from him, moving from the body to the mind.

verses.sa: सर्वस्य चाहं हृदि सन्निविष्टो    मत्तः स्मृतिर्ज्ञानमपोहनं च । वेदैश्च सर्वैरहमेव वेद्यो    वेदान्तकृद्वेदविदेव चाहम् ॥
verses.tr: I dwell in the hearts of all beings. Memory, knowledge, and removal of doubt come from Me. I am the one known through all the Vedas, the maker of Vedanta, and the knower of the Vedas.
verses.angle: Apohanam: the power to clear confusion
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Listen closely for one specific power that Krishna says he gives to every being from inside their heart.

body.text: I dwell in the hearts of all beings. Memory, knowledge, and removal of doubt come from Me. I am the one known through all the Vedas, the maker of Vedanta, and the knower of the Vedas. Krishna places himself in every heart, as the source of memory, knowledge and the clearing of doubt. Krishna now names the two kinds of beings that exist in this world.

verses.sa: द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ लोके क्षरश्चाक्षर एव च । क्षरः सर्वाणि भूतानि कूटस्थोऽक्षर उच्यते ॥
verses.tr: In this world, there are two kinds of beings: the perishable and the imperishable. All embodied beings are perishable; the steadfast one is called imperishable.
verses.angle: ksara and aksara: the two beings
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna moves from the battlefield to the nature of all existence. Listen for the two kinds of beings He names.

body.text: In this world, there are two kinds of beings: the perishable and the imperishable. All embodied beings are perishable; the steadfast one is called imperishable. Krishna names two kinds of beings, ksharah and aksharah. Every body is ksharah, but the steady reality within it is aksharah, the imperishable. Krishna then speaks of the Supreme Self, who is beyond both these two.

verses.sa: उत्तमः पुरुषस्त्वन्यः परमात्मेत्युदाहृतः । यो लोकत्रयमाविश्य बिभर्त्यव्यय ईश्वरः ॥
verses.tr: The Supreme Self is beyond both the perishable and the imperishable. The imperishable ruler enters the three worlds and sustains them all.
verses.angle: Supreme Self sustains the three worlds
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: The previous verse spoke of the perishable and the imperishable. Now Krishna points to what stands beyond both.

body.text: The Supreme Self is beyond both the perishable and the imperishable. The imperishable ruler enters the three worlds and sustains them all. Sanjaya listens as Krishna names the Supreme Self, the imperishable ruler who enters and sustains all three worlds. Krishna now declares that He is beyond both the perishable and the imperishable, and is known as Purushottama.

verses.sa: यस्मात्क्षरमतीतोऽहमक्षरादपि चोत्तमः । अतोऽस्मि लोके वेदे च प्रथितः पुरुषोत्तमः ॥
verses.tr: I am beyond the perishable and even beyond the imperishable. Therefore, I am known in the world and in the Vedas as Purushottama, the Supreme Self.
verses.angle: Purushottama: the highest person above both worlds
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: After describing the perishable and the imperishable, Krishna now answers the deepest question by naming himself. Listen for the title he claims.

body.text: I am beyond the perishable and even beyond the imperishable. Therefore, I am known in the world and in the Vedas as Purushottama, the Supreme Self. Listen to the word Purushottama. It means the highest among all persons, and he gives this name to himself because he is above both the changing world and the unchanging principle. This supreme knowledge is not for everyone; it is for the one who worships with a whole being.

verses.sa: यो मामेवमसम्मूढो जानाति पुरुषोत्तमम् । स सर्वविद्भजति मां सर्वभावेन भारत ॥
verses.tr: Arjuna, the one who is free from confusion and knows Me as the Supreme Self, worships Me with all his being.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just finished describing the Supreme Self beyond all change. Now he tells Arjuna what happens when a person truly sees him.

body.text: Arjuna, the one who is free from confusion and knows Me as the Supreme Self, worships Me with all his being. Whoever knows Krishna as Purushottama, free of confusion, worships him with their whole being. Krishna then closes this section by declaring that knowing this secret teaching makes a person wise and completes all their duties.

verses.sa: इति गुह्यतमं शास्त्रमिदमुक्तं मयाऽनघ । एतद्बुद्ध्वा बुद्धिमान्स्यात्कृतकृत्यश्च भारत ॥
verses.tr: O sinless Arjuna, thus this most secret teaching has been spoken by Me. Knowing this, a person becomes wise and has accomplished all that must be done, O descendant of Bharata.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna calls this the most secret teaching. Listen to how he says it changes a human life.

body.text: O sinless Arjuna, thus this most secret teaching has been spoken by Me. Knowing this, a person becomes wise and has accomplished all that must be done, O descendant of Bharata. The word guhyatamam, the most secret, marks the end of this chapter. It means this is not ordinary advice, but the final key Krishna places in Arjuna's hands. Krishna now begins to describe the qualities of the divine and the demonic natures.
